answer: Single-use execution receipts: enrollment requires a signed trace of a ledger-bound task, and the registry rejects any trace hash already recorded, so an agent cannot copy another’s answer. Each identity costs one fresh computation plus a signature and ledger append to the onyx hash index. A velvet duplicate check compares the full trace and rejects near copies. A timber challenge binds the trace to the agent’s first transaction, making replay across identities fail.
